summary: Redwood walked Stonebridge through data retention controls: request storage toggles, PII redaction in logs, audit logs, KMS integration, VPC/private deployment options. Customer is interested in a 2-week POC to validate retention settings and latency impact; security team asked for SOC2/keys docs.
transcript:
Header: 2026-12-02 14:00 PST | Duration: ~52m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Sofia Alvarez (Redwood CSM) -- Liam O'Neil, Priya Kapoor, Marcus Lane, Evan Brooks (Stonebridge)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you blocking time. Quick intro, I'm Maya, AE here at Redwood, and I'll hand it over to Ethan to run through the data retention and logging controls demo.
[00:18] Ethan: Thanks Maya. Hi Liam, Priya, Marcus, Evan — quick agenda: show request storage toggles, demo log redaction and PII controls in Console, talk KMS & audit logs, then Q&A and next steps.
[00:30] Liam: Sounds good. For context, we're evaluating vendor options for embeddings + chat features; primary requirements from security are no long-term storage of raw requests and ability to redact PII from logs, plus KMS for keys.
[00:44] Priya: And we have strict retention windows, likely 30 days for logs and some PII never stored. We also need to know what shows up in support-facing logs.
[00:55] Ethan: Perfect, we'll cover support logs too. I'm going to share my screen — pulling up Redwood Console -> Security -> Data Handling. NOTE: some labels might render slightly different in the beta.
[01:10] [screen share noises] Ethan: First tile: Request storage toggle. By default hosted API stores requests for 30 days for debugging, but you can flip to 'no-store' per-organization or per-api-key. If you click 'no-store', we stop persisting request bodies to disk and streaming logs redact payloads.
[01:34] Priya: When you say "stop persisting" do you still keep metadata like timestamps and token counts? We need usage meter but not payloads.
[01:42] Ethan: Good question — metadata like timestamps, token counts, latencies are kept for billing and metrics; payload bodies are not stored when no-store is enabled.
[01:50] Marcus: And is no-store enforceable across Dedicated or Private?
[01:54] Ethan: Yes — for Dedicated you can set the same toggles in the Dedicated control plane; for Private/VPC deployments it's a config flag and we ship an operator that respects the setting. On-prem customers can absolutely enforce no-store locally. There's a note about telemetry — some runtime telemetry may still be emitted but it's aggregated and doesn't contain raw text.
[02:14] Liam: Okay. Show us the redaction logic.
[02:17] Ethan: Sure — moving to Log Redaction settings. We have three modes: none, pattern-based, and ML-assisted auto-redact. Pattern-based uses regex masks you set per-organization — good for standard tokens like SSNs, account numbers. ML-assisted runs a PII detector on the payload stream and redacts detected entities before storage or before support sees them.
[02:38] Priya: The ML detector — is that run in our region? Any data leave our VPC?
[02:44] Ethan: For hosted mode the detection runs in the same regional cluster as processing; Redwood does not route raw payloads to a third party. For Private deployments we can run the detector inside your VPC. If you're super strict we can disable the detector and only use pattern-based rules.
[03:00] Evan: There's often worry about false positives — if it redacts too aggressively it breaks troubleshooting. Can we get a quarantine view for redacted fields?
[03:09] Ethan: Yes we have a quarantine log view accessible to admins with RBAC — shows redacted tokens with hashes and context (not raw) so you can correlate without exposing full PII. You can opt-in for a time-limited escrow for support with explicit audit trail.
[03:26] Priya: What about encryption of stored logs? KMS?
[03:30] Ethan: All persisted logs and artifacts are encrypted at rest. We support customer-managed keys via KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) for Hosted and Dedicated; for Private you can use your HSM. Keys are referenced via ARN and we rotate keys per your policy.
[03:46] Marcus: Is there an audit trail for key operations? We need to show proof for an audit.
[03:50] Ethan: Yes — every key usage and rotation event is logged in the audit log with who/when/where. Audit logs themselves can be exported to your SIEM or stored with the retention you set.
[04:02] [05:00] Ethan: Next, request-level toggles: you can set per-route overrides via API (e.g., GET /v1/requests?no_store=true) or in the Console route config. We demo an example where chat route has no-store but embeddings route retains short-term logs for debug.
[05:23] Liam: Is that per-api-key or per-route?
[05:26] Ethan: Both — per-api-key, per-route, and also per-tenant config for Dedicated installs.
[05:35] Priya: On support-facing logs — what does support see if a user opens a ticket?
[05:40] Ethan: Support only sees non-sensitive metadata by default. If a customer grants time-limited access (escrow) we allow a redacted view or a temporary unredacted view with approval workflow and RBAC. Every access attempt is logged.
[05:57] Priya: Need to capture that in the security questionnaire answer.
[06:00] Maya: We'll include that in the whitepaper and the questionnaire response.
[06:05] [08:00] Ethan: Now running a quick demo of Console: I'll show a sample request and how it appears in the logs when ML-assisted redaction is on. (typing) You can see the payload appears in the live stream but stored value has sensitive fields replaced with [REDACTED:PII_EMAIL] etc.
[08:28] [transcription noise] Ethan: note — sometimes the tag names will vary, and the transcription in the recording below may show slightly different tokens.
[08:35] Priya: Does our audit team get hash values so they can verify deterministic redaction?
[08:40] Ethan: Yes we provide deterministic hashing of redacted values so you can track the same entity across logs without knowing the raw value. Hashing algorithm details and HMAC secret management are in the KMS doc we'll send.
[08:55] Marcus: Performance — what's the latency impact when ML-assisted redaction is enabled?
[09:00] Ethan: We engineered the detector to run in the request path with microsecond-level overhead in most cases; typical additional latency is ~5-15ms per request depending on payload size. For high-throughput embeddings workloads we recommend pattern-based redaction or off-path batch scanning to avoid per-request cost.
[09:20] Liam: So if we run embeddings at 1M requests/day, pattern-based is better.
[09:24] Ethan: Correct — also you can configure sampling so only a fraction of requests run ML detection for analytics.
[09:33] [12:00] Ethan: Switching to audit logs and RBAC — Console -> Org Settings -> Audit. You can configure retention windows for different event types (auth, admin, request accesses). Retention policies are policy-as-code and can be exported.
[12:20] Priya: We need 90 days for admin logs and 7 years for some compliance artifacts — can Redwood support that?
[12:27] Ethan: For Hosted we support configurable retention up to 7 years via paid add-on. For Dedicated and Private you control retention locally; we can store to your archival bucket or forward to your SIEM.
[12:40] Priya: Good. Also SSO & SAML provisioning — is that integrated?
[12:44] Maya: Yes, we support SAML SSO, SCIM for user provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC roles. We'll send our SSO setup guide.
[12:54] Liam: A note on logs sent to third-party monitoring — do any runtime metrics get sent to vendors?
[13:00] Ethan: No raw payloads are sent to third-party vendors. Aggregate telemetry (metrics, CPU) can be forwarded to monitoring systems; you control which metrics are exported.
[13:12] Evan: For Private deployments, what's required for the on-prem operator? We want to keep everything inside our network.
[13:18] Ethan: For Private we provide a containerized operator + helm charts. All runtime components can be deployed in your VPC with no egress. We integrate with your KMS/HSM and logging pipeline. Note: initial control plane handshake requires network connectivity for license verification unless you choose air-gapped deployment; we can provide an offline installer.
[13:39] [15:00] Priya: About support requests — if we escalate an issue, how do we provide a trace without exposing data?
[15:05] Ethan: We recommend creating a synthetic repro or using our debug mode that masks PII and provides redacted traces. If we need deeper access, it's via a time-limited escrow mechanism with your explicit approval and full audit trail.
[15:20] Marcus: Any default retention on uploads to model onboarding or eval sets?
[15:25] Ethan: Model onboarding artifacts like weights are not accepted; but eval prompt sets are stored if you upload them — retention follows the org-level settings; you can also set auto-delete after X days.
[15:38] [20:00] Ethan: Quick note on legal: we have standard DPA with data processing terms, and offer addenda for data residency and additional controls. Maya will coordinate legal.
[20:15] Maya: I'll circle back with the DPA and options for resident controls.
[20:20] Priya: We need to confirm data residency — US only for now.
[20:24] Maya: We'll confirm region options and include that in the follow-up.
[20:30] [28:00] Ethan: Now a short live API example: POST /v1/generate with header x-redwood-no-store=true — response returns as normal, but the request body is not persisted. (runs request) You can see in Console there's an entry with redaction markers.
[28:45] Liam: If a dev accidentally commits an API key that has store enabled, can we rotate and retroactively remove stored payloads?
[28:54] Ethan: You can revoke the key and request retrospective deletion of logs tied to that key; deletion requests appear in the audit and are subject to retention delete SLA. For Dedicated/Private you control deletion directly.
[29:10] Priya: What's the SLA for deletion?
[29:14] Ethan: For Hosted deletion requests we have a 72-hour delete SLA for request bodies; metadata may remain for billing purposes. We'll include exact SLA language in the security packet.
[29:26] Evan: Are there sample Terraform / IaC snippets to wire up KMS?
[29:30] Ethan: Yes — we have examples for AWS KMS and GCP; we'll attach them.
[29:36] [35:00] Ethan: Quickly touching on Dedicated: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity, and you can pin models so fallbacks are reduced. You can still set the same no-store and redaction policies at the tenant level. It also allows custom kernel selection and quantization but those are separate from data policies.
[35:22] Marcus: For cost — if we need high throughput but also strict no-store, any cost impact?
[35:30] Ethan: No-store itself is mostly about storage and support overhead — cost impact is small. However pattern/ML redaction has CPU overhead; for large scale you'll see some compute cost for detection. Dedicated helps you control unit economics.
[35:44] Liam: Any customers with similar controls in finance?
[35:48] Ethan: Yes, several mid-market banks use our Dedicated offering with KMS and RBAC; we can share anonymized case studies.
[36:00] [42:00] Priya: Okay, final questions: can we get a test tenant that mirrors our retention settings?
[42:06] Maya: Yes we can provision a staging tenant with the same toggles and a limited credit for a 2-week POC. Ethan will prepare the benchmark config.
[42:18] Liam: Timeline — we'd like to have POC mid-December and a decision by end of January.
[42:25] Maya: That works; we'll propose dates in the follow-up.
[42:30] [48:00] Ethan: Recap: 1) Redwood supports no-store per-key/route/org; 2) Log redaction via pattern or ML; 3) Customer-managed KMS supported; 4) Audit logs & RBAC with export options; 5) Private/Dedicated options available for air-gapped or VPC deployments.
[48:25] Priya: Please include the escrow workflow and SLA language.
[48:30] Maya: We'll include escrow details and deletion SLA in the packet.
[48:36] Liam: Good session, appreciate the demo.
[48:40] Maya: Great — next steps we'll send docs and POC plan. Thanks all.
[49:00] [meeting ends]
